targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: 2030 is Eurostat's stated aim, not a locked legal date — the ESA 2030 proposal is still in consultation.

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (www.ibge.gov.br contas-nacionais path, plain curl, HTTP 200, 132,905 bytes — this path served genuine bytes where the PNAD Contínua path on the same host returned a WAF 403). IBGE's own page: "As informações da série do Sistema de Contas Nacionais - referência 2010, cabe ressaltar, são apresentadas segundo uma classificação de produtos e atividades integrada com a Classificação Nacional de Atividades Econômicas - CNAE 2.0 e estão em conformidade com o System of national accounts 2008, SNA 2008, manual preparado sob os auspícios da Organização das Nações Unidas - ONU, da Comissão Europeia - Eurostat, do Fundo Monetário Internacional - FMI, da Organização de Cooperação e Desenvolvimento Econômico - OCDE e do Banco Mundial, o que reflete o compromisso do IBGE com a sistemática de revisões periódicas de suas práticas, conforme preconizam as recomendações internacionais." "Em conformidade com" is a methodology claim, not a citation for context, and the sentence names the manual, its edition and its five sponsoring bodies. Brazil's first edge into the international-standards.json layer, and the same shape the corpus already carries for Canadian, German and Antipodean national accounts. Note that sna-2008 is itself superseded by the 2025 SNA per its own node description, with country rollout targeting 2029-2030; IBGE's current rebasing exercise (reference year moving from 2010 to 2021) is the natural moment for that transition, but IBGE's page states only the rebasing, not an SNA edition change, so nothing is asserted about it here.

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A (www.ibge.gov.br contas-nacionais path, plain curl, HTTP 200, 151,398 bytes). IBGE's own page for the quarterly accounts: "As estimativas das CNT seguem as recomendações internacionais reunidas no mais recente manual das Nações Unidas - Sistema de Contas Nacionais (SNA 2008). Todas as transações definidas no SNA para a produção (transações mercantis e não mercantis) são registradas em regime de competência, exceto as receitas do governo, que são registradas em regime de caixa." The second sentence is what makes this `methodology_depends_on` beyond doubt: it does not merely claim conformity, it applies a specific SNA recording rule (accrual for production, cash for government receipts) and states its own exception to it. An independent statement from the quarterly programme rather than an inheritance from the annual one, so it is minted as its own edge rather than assumed through br-cnt -> br-scn.

results.window:
The Full Story

 The Statistical Institute of Jamaica (STATIN) is reporting that the Jamaican System of National Accounts has been updated to reflect international best practices, enhancing comparability and analytic relevance. The revisions to the Jamaican System of National Accounts include aligning the national accounts with the United Nations System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008), adoption of the 2016 revision of the Jamaica Industrial Classification (JIC 2016), rebasing constant (real) price estimates from 2007 to 2015; and incorporating new and revised data into the gross domestic product (GDP) estimates. Acting Director of the Economic Accounting Division, STATIN, Walata Wallace, provided details on the changes during a virtual Economic Statistics Media Stakeholders Meeting on the revision to the Jamaica System of National Accounts, on July 3.

Over the past three years, five normative acts were adopted by the President of the Republic
of Uzbekistan, as well as more than 30 regulatory provisions focused on their
implementation were adopted by the government. The list and composition of the published statistical information have been increased, the
Republic has joined the IMF’s enhanced General Data Dissemination System and the
functioning of the open data portal has been improved both in terms of the quality of
information and its content. As a result of these reforms, the produced data are highly relevant, in-demand, more open
and accessible to society, which better satisfies user requests for statistical information and
increases confidence in official statistics.

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and a documented instance of the supranational-to-national dependency REPORTS.md's own secondary objective is looking for -- a national statistical system stating, in its own text, that it was revised to conform to an international standard. Verbatim: 「2009年，联合国等五大国际组织颁布了国民经济核算新的国际标准——《国民账户体系2008》（以下简称2008年SNA）。目前，绝大部分发达国家和部分发展中国家已经开始执行2008年SNA。我国国民经济核算体系也需要做出相应的修订，使之与新的国际标准相衔接，提高国际可比性。」 ("In 2009, the United Nations and four other major international organisations promulgated the new international standard for national economic accounting — the System of National Accounts 2008 … China's national economic accounting system also needs to be revised accordingly, so as to align with the new international standard and improve international comparability.") The operative clause repeats the intent constitutively: 「实现与国民经济核算新的国际标准相衔接…我国对中国国民经济核算体系进行了全面系统的修订。」 TENSE NOTE, flagged because the sentence mixes them: the promulgation of the 2008 SNA is described in the past, but the alignment is stated in present-constitutive voice (「使之与新的国际标准相衔接」 — "so as to align it with the new international standard"), and the revision it justifies is the instrument being issued. The edge is sound on the alignment clause, not on the historical one. Unlike most China edges this round, the target is named by exact title AND edition year, so there is no version ambiguity of the kind that blocked the COICOP edge (see `_dropped`).

targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. results.basis: Destatis states ESA 2010 as the legal basis of the German national accounts in the structured metadata of its own quality report: 'Scope of the statistics: national accounts of the Federation (EVAS No 81) … Legal bases: Regulation (EC) No 549/2013, European System of National and Regional Accounts (ESA) 2010, and supplementary and amending regulations … Periodicity: quarterly, annual'. The same report sets out the mechanism: 'The ESA 2010 is a European Regulation, which is binding for all EU member states as of 1 September 2014 (Council Regulation (EU) No. 549/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 21 May 2013, published in the Official Journal on 26 June 2013). It was implemented in Germany as part of the 2014 general revision. This regulation was amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/734 …'. Two further documents say the same in their own words: the GNI inventory ('in compliance with the European System of National Accounts (ESA) 2010' and 'based on the European System of Accounts (ESA) 2010') and the QNA inventory ('in compliance with the European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)'). relationship_type is methodology_depends_on rather than uses_data_from: ESA 2010 supplies no figures, it supplies the 'common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables' (Regulation 549/2013, Article 1(2)(a)).

targetReport.title: System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008)
targetReport.publisher: United Nations, European Commission, IMF, OECD and World Bank
targetReport.description: The internationally agreed standard set of concepts, definitions, classifications and accounting rules for compiling national accounts, in force 2008-2025. Superseded by the 2025 SNA (UNSC 56th Session, March 2025) — see sna-2025. Retained here because the eight reports below still cite it by name as their methodology basis; country-level rollout of the successor targets 2029-2030, so nothing downstream is factually wrong yet.
targetReport.cadence_note: Revised roughly once a generation — previous editions 1953, 1968 and 1993. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal so the pulse rate reads as near-static.

release_schedule.note: Superseded by the 2025 SNA (UNSC 56th Session, March 2025) — see sna-2025's own published-calendar schedule for the adoption date and rollout window. No further revisions expected under the SNA 2008 edition.

results.basis: Council Regulation (EC) No 479/2009, consolidated text of 01/09/2014, Article 1(1): 'For the purposes of the Protocol on the excessive deficit procedure and of this Regulation, the terms in paragraphs 2 to 6 are defined according to Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 of the European Parliament and the Council of 21 May 2013 on the European system of national and regional accounts in the European Union (hereinafter referred to as ESA 2010). The codes in brackets refer to ESA 2010.' The dependence is operative, not decorative: Article 1(2) defines 'Government' as 'the sector of general government (S.13)... as defined in ESA 2010', Article 1(3) defines 'Government deficit (surplus)' as 'the net borrowing (net lending) (B.9) of the sector of general government (S.13), as defined in ESA 2010', and Article 1(5) defines 'Government debt' by ESA 2010 categories 'currency and deposits (AF.2); debt securities (AF.3) and loans (AF.4)'. 'Are defined according to' is derivation language and is not on Research.1.md section 5a's watchlist. Direction: the EDP Regulation is the dependent, ESA 2010 the depended-on. Re-fetched and re-read from EUR-Lex 2026-08-07 after G.50.md Finding 4 recorded the site serving nothing; the outage was transient. Quoted with EUR-Lex's in-line amendment markers stripped — the unstripped Article 1(1) reads with the whole clause inside a M2 insertion marker, because the original 2009 text referred to ESA 95.

Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.

results.window:
The Hellenic Statistical Authority (ELSTAT) announces the fiscal data for the years 2015-2018 compiled in the context
of the second Excessive Deficit Procedure (EDP) notification of 2019, which was transmitted to Eurostat in fulfilment
of Greece’s obligations according to Council Regulation (EC) 479/2009 as amended. These data have been produced
on the basis of the new Regulation ESA 2010 (549/2013) for the System of National Accounts, which became
obligatory as of 01.09.2014. The surplus of General Government for 2018, in accordance with ESA 2010, is estimated at 1.8 billion euro (1% of
Gross Domestic Product), while the gross consolidated General Government debt at year-end 2018 is estimated at a
nominal value of 334.7 billion euro (181.2% of Gross Domestic Product).

Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: 2030 is Eurostat's stated aim, not a locked legal date — the ESA 2030 proposal is still in consultation.

results.window: As for the other factors, they are related to changes in the quality and quantity of goods and services and the amounts spent on them. Therefore, the consumer price index is a measure of price changes only and not a measure of changes in the cost of living. The consumer price index also differs from the retail price index, in that the latter relates to the prices of all goods that are included in retail trade, while the interest in the consumer price index is focused on the goods and services purchased by the consumer, as it is limited only to measuring the change during a period of time.

Description

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, edition named, and it closes the question BRICS/G.2 had to leave open. Chapter 2's opening sentence: "As per recommendations of System of National Accounts (SNA)-2008, NAD industry-wise estimates of GDP are compiled using institutional sector approach. All resident institutional units are allocated to one and only one of the following five institutional sectors: i. The non-financial corporation sector; ii. The financial corporation sector; iii. The general government sector; ..." The edition is explicit, the compiler named is the National Accounts Division itself, and the claim is about how India's GDP estimates ARE compiled rather than how they might be. `methodology_depends_on`: "as per recommendations of" introduces the sectoral framework actually used. THE SCOPE LIMIT IS THE REASON THIS EDGE IS MINTED FROM A NEW NODE RATHER THAN FROM `in-mospi-nas`: the quote is from a companion methodology report of the National Accounts Division, not from the body of the National Accounts Statistics publication, whose own release text still says only "System of National Accounts (SNA)" with no year. Attaching the edge to `in-mospi-nas` would put a citation in that node's mouth that its document does not make -- so the report is minted as its own node instead, exactly as the Russian side handles `ru-rosstat-osm-233-household-accounts`. Secondary corroboration in the same PDF (§1.1, "consistent with the System of National Accounts (SNA) guidelines") is unversioned and would not support an edge alone.

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, from an Indian-authored, Indian-hosted primary document -- which is what the evidence standard requires, an IMF-side claim of Indian coverage would not qualify. Annex II: "India has also been disseminating data on external debt under the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standards (SDDS) and Quarterly External Debt Statistics (QEDS) database jointly developed by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund." and, operatively: "The external debt statistics of India are disseminated with a lag of three months from the end of the reference quarter in both the country-specific and SDDS format and are accessible at www.finmin.nic.in and www.rbi.org.in." NO EDITION PROBLEM: SDDS is a single named standard rather than an edition series, and the Indian text names it by full title. `methodology_depends_on` because the standard governs the dissemination FORMAT and periodicity actually used -- the dependency is on SDDS's dissemination dimension, stated plainly here rather than implied to be broader.

targetReport.title: European System of Accounts 2010 (ESA 2010)
targetReport.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
targetReport.description: The EU's national accounts framework, enacted as Regulation (EU) No 549/2013. Article 1(2) sets out its two parts: 'a methodology (Annex A) on common standards, definitions, classifications and accounting rules that shall be used for compiling accounts and tables on comparable bases for the purposes of the Union' and 'a programme (Annex B) setting out the time limits by which Member States shall transmit to the Commission (Eurostat) the accounts and tables'. Unlike the international standards already in this corpus, ESA 2010 is a Regulation — member states do not adopt it by choice — which is why the EU branch was expected to produce supranational-to-national edges the Canada/US pair lacks. Annex B turned out to name tables and deadlines rather than publications; see the _dropped entries here and in eu-draft-budget.json.
targetReport.cadence_note: A generational standard, revised roughly once every fifteen to twenty years: ESA 1995 preceded it, and a further revision is already anticipated. releases_per_year matches sna-2008 (0.05) so the two read at the same pulse rate; see _open_questions.

release_schedule.note: 2030 is Eurostat's stated aim, not a locked legal date — the ESA 2030 proposal is still in consultation.

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, with the edition named unambiguously and repeatedly. The methodology's stated purpose is derivation from the standard: «Цель данной методологии – разработка алгоритма формирования показателей нефинансовых счетов сектора домашних хозяйств в системе национальных счетов Российской Федерации на основе Руководства «Система национальных счетов 2008»¹ (далее – СНС 2008).» The footnote gives a full bibliographic citation -- «¹ Система национальных счетов 2008: Пер. с англ. / Еврокомиссия, МВФ, ОЭСР, ООН, Всемирный банк. – Нью-Йорк, 2012.» -- and a terminology note confirms which edition's language is used: «При подготовке документа использована терминология, зафиксированная в русскоязычном издании СНС 2008 года, опубликованном Секретариатом ООН в 2012 году.» «СНС 2008» appears 44 times in the document. `methodology_depends_on` rather than `cites`: «на основе Руководства…» ("on the basis of the Manual") is a derivation claim in a legally approved official statistical methodology, not a background mention. SCOPE WEAKNESS, stated: this is a SECTORAL methodology (household non-financial accounts), so the edge is narrower than "Russian national accounts depend on SNA 2008" in general -- but at least five sibling Rosstat orders make the same citation for other parts of the accounts, several with a stronger conformance verb, and they are listed in `_dropped` so a future round can broaden the coverage without re-researching it.

results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A. Rosstat states that its GDP release timetable is determined by the IMF standard: «Сроки представления данных по ВВП публикуются в «Федеральном плане статистических работ» и соответствуют срокам публикации этого показателя, определенным Специальным стандартом распространения данных МВФ, к которому присоединилась Россия 31 января 2005 года.» ("The release dates for GDP data … correspond to the publication deadlines for this indicator ESTABLISHED BY the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard, to which Russia acceded on 31 January 2005.") NO EDITION PROBLEM: the SDDS is a single named standard rather than an edition series, the corpus holds one `imf-sdds` node, and the Russian text names it in full («Специальный стандарт распространения данных МВФ») and pins the accession date. `methodology_depends_on` because the dependency is real and operative, with the scope stated honestly: it is a dependency on the SDDS's TIMELINESS dimension -- what must be published when -- not on GDP concepts, which come from the SNA. results.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, TIER A, and structurally the strongest dependency in the Russian branch even though it is typed conservatively. The SDDS appears in the ENABLING PREAMBLE of a numbered, Minjust-registered Minfin order -- part of the legal authority under which the government-finance-statistics procedure is issued, not a methodological reference: «…постановления Правительства Российской Федерации от 26 сентября 1997 г. № 1226 "О присоединении Российской Федерации к Специальному стандарту распространения данных МВФ" …, в целях совершенствования методологии формирования информации по статистике государственных финансов п р и к а з ы в а ю:». The standard's full Russian name appears verbatim in the order's own text, so the requirement that the dependent document name the standard itself is satisfied, even though the immediate instrument cited is the 1997 Government Resolution effecting accession. `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on` DELIBERATELY: the SDDS here supplies legal authority and a transmission obligation (the Порядок §22 requires Treasury transmission «в Международный валютный фонд» on a fixed timetable), while the compilation METHOD the order actually prescribes is described only by unversioned reference to «руководствами по распространению (раскрытию) данных» -- so a methodology-typed edge would overstate what this document says. A TENSE/EVENT NOTE worth preserving: Постановление № 1226 is dated 1997 while Rosstat's GDP procedure gives Russia's SDDS accession as 31 January 2005. These are two different events -- the 1997 resolution authorises accession, 2005 is the subscription date -- and they are not contradictory.

targetReport.description: The IMF's data-dissemination tier for countries not on the (stricter) SDDS/SDDS Plus standards already in the graph. Kenya implemented e-GDDS (with a National Summary Data Page) around 2018, per the IMF's own DSBB e-GDDS pages and confirmed via a related IMF press release. A notch below South Africa and Egypt, both confirmed on full SDDS -- worth having as a distinct node so the graph can actually show the tiering rather than treating every country's IMF dissemination status as equivalent.
targetReport.cadence_note: Standard itself revised rarely; not an annual release, matching the treatment given to imf-sdds.

release_schedule.note: Standing reporting framework, not a periodic release — no schedule to state. This report's own url field previously pointed to a Kenya-specific DQAF sub-page — corrected here to the e-GDDS framework overview page. (Note: the ke-knbs-cpi -> imf-e-gdds edge's evidence_url, the same Kenya-specific page, is left as-is — that citation is correct evidence for that specific edge's claim.)

targetReport.title: IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)
targetReport.publisher: International Monetary Fund
targetReport.description: The IMF's voluntary standard for the coverage, periodicity, timeliness and advance-release-calendar practices of a country's official statistics. A parallel edge for Canada (`statcan-cpi -> imf-sdds-plus`, the stricter SDDS Plus tier) was scoped and dropped in `international-frameworks.json` for lack of national-side evidence -- every document naming the obligation was IMF-side, none from StatCan itself. South Africa has the national-side evidence Canada's case lacked: Stats SA's own CPI Sources and Methods report states plainly, 'The South African CPI complies with the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)' -- the plain SDDS tier, not SDDS Plus, and not independently checked against South Africa's actual IMF DSBB country page this session (that page's landing view did not surface country-specific content when fetched directly).
targetReport.cadence_note: Standard itself revised rarely; not an annual release.

release_schedule.note: Framework reviewed 'at intervals determined by the Executive Board' — no fixed periodicity. Last review concluded 2022-03-16 per the IMF's own site. This report's own url field previously pointed to a Statistics South Africa PDF with no connection to the IMF — corrected here to the DSBB SDDS overview page. (Note: the za-statssa-cpi -> imf-sdds edge's evidence_url, the same statssa PDF, is left as-is — that citation is correct evidence for that specific edge's claim.)

targetReport.description: The IMF's data-dissemination tier for countries not on the (stricter) SDDS/SDDS Plus standards already in the graph. Kenya implemented e-GDDS (with a National Summary Data Page) around 2018, per the IMF's own DSBB e-GDDS pages and confirmed via a related IMF press release. A notch below South Africa and Egypt, both confirmed on full SDDS -- worth having as a distinct node so the graph can actually show the tiering rather than treating every country's IMF dissemination status as equivalent.
targetReport.cadence_note: Standard itself revised rarely; not an annual release, matching the treatment given to imf-sdds.

release_schedule.note: Standing reporting framework, not a periodic release — no schedule to state. This report's own url field previously pointed to a Kenya-specific DQAF sub-page — corrected here to the e-GDDS framework overview page. (Note: the ke-knbs-cpi -> imf-e-gdds edge's evidence_url, the same Kenya-specific page, is left as-is — that citation is correct evidence for that specific edge's claim.)

results.basis: IMF, 'Tunisia: 2024 Annual Observance Report of the Special Data Dissemination Standard': 'Tunisia subscribed to the SDDS on June 20, 2001, and met all the SDDS requirements at the time of subscription,' listing 'Price index: Consumer prices' as a monitored monthly category. The same report documents a 2024 timeliness lapse for this category, attributed to a December 2024 SDMX platform migration -- graded as 'cites' rather than 'methodology_depends_on' because this is the IMF's own external assessment, not a first-person compliance statement in INS's own CPI documents.

targetReport.title: IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)
targetReport.publisher: International Monetary Fund
targetReport.description: The IMF's voluntary standard for the coverage, periodicity, timeliness and advance-release-calendar practices of a country's official statistics. A parallel edge for Canada (`statcan-cpi -> imf-sdds-plus`, the stricter SDDS Plus tier) was scoped and dropped in `international-frameworks.json` for lack of national-side evidence -- every document naming the obligation was IMF-side, none from StatCan itself. South Africa has the national-side evidence Canada's case lacked: Stats SA's own CPI Sources and Methods report states plainly, 'The South African CPI complies with the IMF Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS)' -- the plain SDDS tier, not SDDS Plus, and not independently checked against South Africa's actual IMF DSBB country page this session (that page's landing view did not surface country-specific content when fetched directly).
targetReport.cadence_note: Standard itself revised rarely; not an annual release.

release_schedule.note: Framework reviewed 'at intervals determined by the Executive Board' — no fixed periodicity. Last review concluded 2022-03-16 per the IMF's own site. This report's own url field previously pointed to a Statistics South Africa PDF with no connection to the IMF — corrected here to the DSBB SDDS overview page. (Note: the za-statssa-cpi -> imf-sdds edge's evidence_url, the same statssa PDF, is left as-is — that citation is correct evidence for that specific edge's claim.)

 Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board of Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan)

Welcome to the Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board of Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (DSBB/CBC). The DSBB/CBC provides most information on the financial and external sectors of the Republic of China about the Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS), which was established by the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in 1996 to guide countries that have, or that might seek, access to international capital markets in the dissemination of economic and financial data to the public. DSBB:

The IMF's Dissemination Standards Bulletin Board which provides information about SDDS.

targetReport.title: System of National Accounts 2008 (SNA 2008)
targetReport.publisher: United Nations, European Commission, IMF, OECD and World Bank
targetReport.description: The internationally agreed standard set of concepts, definitions, classifications and accounting rules for compiling national accounts, in force 2008-2025. Superseded by the 2025 SNA (UNSC 56th Session, March 2025) — see sna-2025. Retained here because the eight reports below still cite it by name as their methodology basis; country-level rollout of the successor targets 2029-2030, so nothing downstream is factually wrong yet.
targetReport.cadence_note: Revised roughly once a generation — previous editions 1953, 1968 and 1993. Not an annual release; releases_per_year is nominal so the pulse rate reads as near-static.

release_schedule.note: Superseded by the 2025 SNA (UNSC 56th Session, March 2025) — see sna-2025's own published-calendar schedule for the adoption date and rollout window. No further revisions expected under the SNA 2008 edition.

results.basis: IMF Country Report No. 24/290 (Uganda: Staff Report for the 2024 Article IV Consultation, Informational Annex), Annex V 'Data Issues', Table 2: 'Uganda participates in the Enhanced General Data Dissemination System (e-GDDS) and publishes the data on its National Summary Data Page since November 2016.' Corroborated structurally by the IMF's own DSBB e-GDDS participants list (which includes Uganda) and its SDDS subscriber list (which does not). Reuses the imf-e-gdds node, placing Uganda on the same weaker dissemination tier already confirmed for Kenya, Nigeria, Ethiopia and Ghana, rather than the stronger SDDS tier confirmed for South Africa, Egypt and Tanzania.

results.basis: Vietnam's official National Summary Data Page (nsdp.nso.gov.vn), the IMF e-GDDS portal for Vietnam, states: "Data linked from this page correspond to data described in the International Monetary Fund’s DSBB. For a fuller explanation of the DSBB and the enhanced General Data Dissemination System in which Vietnam participates, please visit the DSBB home page." SBV is itself a designated data-provider agency on this page — its own Central Bank Survey metadata document, filed on the same NSDP and used to compile reserve-money and other monetary statistics, names "The State Bank of Vietnam" as the reporting agency ("Reserve money is compiled on a monthly basis by the State Bank of Vietnam (SBV)"). This complements the existing vn-gso -> imf-e-gdds edge: GSO and SBV are separate e-GDDS-participating agencies filing their own category's metadata within the same Vietnamese national framework.
